papers.authors: Blades RB, Boyle CC, Eisenberger NI, Cole SW, Korecki JRT, Fuligni AJ, Bower JE.
papers.design: Randomized controlled trial; registered single-blind (outcome assessors)
papers.summary: After six weeks, the meditation group showed lower neural responses to social-evaluative threat and lower inferred NF-κB activity. The gene-regulation difference lost statistical significance after adjustment for the neural-response change.
papers.limitation: A small waitlist-controlled trial. Promoter analysis estimates transcription-factor activity; the analysis does not establish a causal neural mechanism.

studyDesignAssessment.basis: The linked trial register specifies masked outcome assessors; participants knew their allocation.

papers.title: Psychological assessments, allostatic load and gene expression analyses in a randomized controlled trial comparing meditation, yoga, and stress education
papers.authors: Denninger JW, Joss D, Romero PM, Khalsa SBS, Hoge EA, Bhasin M, Lazar SW, Dusek JA, Macklin E, Libermann T, Fricchione GL, Benson H.
papers.design: Randomized controlled trial; registered double-blind (participants and outcome assessors)
papers.summary: The three-arm trial found no significant between-group effects on psychological, genomic or allostatic-load outcomes. Most psychological measures improved within each group. Circulating IL-6 increased slightly within the meditation group at follow-up, remaining in the normal range.
papers.limitation: Within-group improvement does not establish a treatment advantage. Participants were stressed but otherwise healthy; results may differ in clinical populations.

studyDesignAssessment.basis: The linked trial register specifies double masking of participants and outcome assessors. The article does not describe the masking procedure; this classification reflects the registered design.

evidence.sample: 211 chronically stressed adults: 73 meditation, 68 yoga, 70 control
evidence.measurement: Blood gene-expression measures and allostatic-load biomarkers
evidence.reviewScope: Publication abstract and selected full-text methods; Jadad assessment pending
